newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: South Korea takes steps to boost stock market.
newsitem.headline: South Korea takes steps to boost stock market.

text.p: South Korea plans to allow domestic investment firms to issue between $1 billion and $1.2 billion of beneficiary certificates to foreigners in stocks and bonds this year, the finance ministry said on Tuesday.
This compares with $900 million in 1996, a ministry statement said. A finance ministry official said the move was aimed at boosting the ailing stock market.
The ministry statement encouraged investment firms to submit their issue plans by the end of February.
Those that issue certificates in February will be given preference for future issues this year.
To help boost sales of the certificates, the ratio of stock investment in each underlying equity-type fund will be lowered to a maximum 70 percent from 80 percent, the statement said.
